Messages.Body:
A few question seems to arise time and again .. and I can't really seem
to be able to track them down with the usual Google search, even though
I'm quite certain they have been asked and answered before, so here
goes:

1. Theft of Vitae ... Is this card usable when in combat with an ally?
Or can you only steal blood (not life)?

2. Taste of Vitae ... Is this card only usable when in combat with an
opposing vampire or can you also "taste" blood (life) from an ally. When
tallying the amount of damage inflicted, do you count both damage taken
from 1.The opposing vampire and 2. Enviromental sources (Like Carrion
Crows, etc.)

3. Disarm. When deciding whether a vampire has inflicted "more" damage
at close range or not, is this damage dependent upon damage taken/given
from an opposing vampries strikes or do you also count enviromental
damage into this??

4. Is Taste of Vitae usable at both short and long range?

5. Drawing out the Beast vs. Sniper Rifle ... Which card takes
precendece?? (If the vampire equipped with the Sniper Rifle is the
reacting vampire)??

6. Flesh of Marble. Does FoM "reduce" damage or prevent damage??

7. I know, for sure, this question has been answered quite recently, but
just can't seem to find it anywhere, so I'll just have to ask it again,
now won't I ;) Can the use of temptation interrupt an action, or say in
the middle of combat??

That was it for now ;)

Regards

> 1. Theft of Vitae ... Is this card usable when in combat with an ally?

Yes you can =)
if you use it against a vampire you steal blood, if you use it against an
ally, you steal life. The result is the same.

> 2. Taste of Vitae ... Is this card only usable when in combat with an
> opposing vampire or can you also "taste" blood (life) from an ally. When
> tallying the amount of damage inflicted, do you count both damage taken
> from 1.The opposing vampire and 2. Enviromental sources (Like Carrion
> Crows, etc.)

Only usable against a vampire. Has no effect when used against an ally.
when tallying the damage, you count every point of damage that has not been
prevented, including environmental.

> 3. Disarm. When deciding whether a vampire has inflicted "more" damage
> at close range or not, is this damage dependent upon damage taken/given
> from an opposing vampries strikes or do you also count enviromental
> damage into this??

environmental doesn't count (card text)

> 4. Is Taste of Vitae usable at both short and long range?

yes =)

> 5. Drawing out the Beast vs. Sniper Rifle ... Which card takes
> precendece?? (If the vampire equipped with the Sniper Rifle is the
> reacting vampire)??

Drawing out the beast takes precedence.(opposing vampire cannot use
equipment, played before range is chosen)

> 6. Flesh of Marble. Does FoM "reduce" damage or prevent damage??

it "prevents" all the damage up to the syndical minima of 1. (new card text)

http://www.white-wolf.com/vtes/rulebook/

>2. Taste of Vitae ... Is this card only usable when in combat with an
>opposing vampire or can you also "taste" blood (life) from an ally.

It is only usable when in combat with a vampire.
Pertinent card text:
"lost by the opposing vampire to damage"

> When tallying the amount of damage inflicted, do you count both damage taken
>from 1.The opposing vampire and 2. Enviromental sources (Like Carrion
>Crows, etc.)

This includes all damage inflicted regardless of the source of the
damage.

>3. Disarm. When deciding whether a vampire has inflicted "more" damage
>at close range or not, is this damage dependent upon damage taken/given
>from an opposing vampries strikes or do you also count enviromental
>damage into this??

Disarm only counts the damage done by the vampire. Damage not
directly caused by the vampire is not counted, ie Carrion Crows will
not allow you to Disarm your opponent when you both strike hands for
one.

This is in the FAQ, section 3.17
http://www.thelasombra.com/vtes_faq.htm

>4. Is Taste of Vitae usable at both short and long range?

Yes.
It is not a strike, so its effects ignore the range of the combat.

>5. Drawing out the Beast vs. Sniper Rifle ... Which card takes
>precendece?? (If the vampire equipped with the Sniper Rifle is the
>reacting vampire)??

Drawing out the Beast prevents the reacting vampire from using the
Sniper Rifle.

>6. Flesh of Marble. Does FoM "reduce" damage or prevent damage??

Flesh of Marble prevents damage.

Pertinent Clarified Card Text:

http://www.white-wolf.com/vtes/Cardlist.html

>7. I know, for sure, this question has been answered quite recently, but
>just can't seem to find it anywhere, so I'll just have to ask it again,
>now won't I ;) Can the use of temptation interrupt an action, or say in
>the middle of combat??

Yes.
Temptation can be used at any time during your minion phase.

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:


You can do it after strikes are announced and before strike resolution
(or after resolving a First Strike but before moving on to normal
strike resolution).

The damage applied in combat is handled in combat.

If you attempt to activate Temptation in that period, then the pending
damage is resolved normally and then control changes and combat ends.

Similarly, if you strike with Coma while your Wolf Companion inflicts
1 damage, the opposing minion doesn't escape the damage nor is he denied
the abililty to play Skin of Rock to prevent it. After the damage is
handled, the victim goes to torpor fro the Coma.
